name: The Great War 1914
description: June 1914. The alliances are wound tight, the mobilization timetables are printed, and an archduke is planning a visit to Sarajevo. One spark, or none — the choice may still be yours.

DEU.name: German Empire
DEU.note: Wilhelm II's Germany is Europe's industrial titan, encircled in its own imagination, with a war plan that runs through Belgium.

AUT.name: Austria-Hungary
AUT.note: Eleven nations under one aging crown; Vienna sees Serbian nationalism as an existential poison.

FRA.name: French Republic
FRA.note: The Third Republic drills for revanche; Alsace-Lorraine is a wound that has not closed since 1871.

GBR.name: British Empire
GBR.note: The Royal Navy has won the dreadnought race, but the cabinet is split on continental commitments — and Ireland smolders.

RUS.name: Russian Empire
RUS.note: Nicholas II commands endless manpower on creaking railways; mobilization, once begun, is nearly impossible to stop.

TUR.name: Ottoman Empire
TUR.note: The Young Turks rebuild a battered empire and quietly weigh German offers against old enemies.

ITA.name: Kingdom of Italy
ITA.note: A Triple Alliance member on paper, Rome keeps its options — and its irredentist claims on Austria — very much open.

SRB.name: Kingdom of Serbia
SRB.note: Doubled in size by the Balkan Wars, flush with pan-Slav ambition, and home to secret societies Vienna blames for everything.

USA.name: United States
USA.note: Wilson's America is rich, distant, and determined to stay out of Europe's quarrels — for now.

world.simulationRules: July Crisis logic: alliances are tripwires and mobilization timetables have momentum of their own — but nothing is inevitable; diplomacy can still swerve. If general war comes, it becomes industrial attrition: trenches in the west, vast maneuvers in the east, blockade and U-boats at sea, and home fronts that crack under strain. Neutrals (Italy, the Ottomans, the United States) drift toward whichever side courts or provokes them.
